Amazon Redshift

Source: vignettes/redshift.Rmd
redshift.Rmd

Amazon Redshift is AWS’s hosted SQL data warehouse. Use it to supply analytics data to a Shiny app with each visitor’s own database permissions. oauth_db_redshift() opens a DBI connection for your SQL queries.

This guide signs users in with Microsoft Entra. It needs a Redshift deployment linked to AWS IAM Identity Center, with the two services configured to recognize those users. Your administrator must arrange that connection before the app can use their sign-in.

Try the guided demo

Run shinyOAuthDB::oauth_db_cloud_demo("redshift") in the R console for an editable app. It checks whether your IAM Identity Center integration is ready before asking for the database and Microsoft sign-in settings. You can save a draft while an administrator configures access.

Install odbc, bslib, processx, askpass and the Redshift ODBC 2.x driver. The app waits for Run example query before connecting; stopping it leaves Redshift compute running. See ?oauth_db_cloud_demo for launcher arguments and Getting started for editing the app.

Set up access

In R, run install.packages("odbc"). Install the AWS Redshift ODBC 2.x driver with IdpTokenAuthPlugin support. Ask your administrator to configure Redshift’s IAM Identity Center integration and set up users’ database permissions.

Create an Entra Web app registration with http://localhost:8100 as its redirect URI. Ask the administrator for the OAuth resource and delegated scope this deployment accepts.

Save those values and the app credentials in a local .Renviron file, then restart R:

OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID=your-tenant-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
OAUTHDB_REDSHIFT_RESOURCE=your-redshift-resource
OAUTHDB_REDSHIFT_SCOPE=your-redshift-delegated-scope
Value Where to get it
server AWS Redshift console: cluster or serverless workgroup endpoint, without the port suffix
database Database name in that endpoint’s connection settings
Tenant ID, client ID, secret The Entra Web registration
Resource and scope The administrator who configured IAM Identity Center’s trusted token issuer and application

For Entra, the resource is the accepted API identifier; the scope is the delegated permission exposed by that registration. These values depend on your AWS/Entra integration and aren’t the Redshift hostname. Give this exact resource/scope pair to token_targets as below.

A complete app

Save this as example.R, replacing the server and database:

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

client <- oauth_db_microsoft_client(
  tenant_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_TENANT_ID"),
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  token_targets = list(
    redshift = list(
      resource = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_REDSHIFT_RESOURCE"),
      scopes = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_REDSHIFT_SCOPE")
    )
  )
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  con <- oauth_db_redshift(
    auth$connection,
    server = "cluster.example.eu-west-1.redshift.amazonaws.com",
    database = "reporting",
    target = "redshift"
  )
  output$rows <- renderTable({
    connection <- con()
    DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT current_user AS database_user")
  })
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*"),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at http://localhost:8100
# (viewers in RStudio/Positron/etc. cannot perform necessary redirects)

Run source("example.R") and open http://localhost:8100. Sign in to run the query; signing out clears the output.

The query shows the Redshift database user. Replace it with SQL for a table that user can read. Call con() inside the reactive expression before querying with DBI.

Driver settings

The default driver name is "Amazon Redshift (x64)". Set driver if your installed driver has a different name or path. You can also pass CaFile and LoginTimeout to the driver. The helper configures token authentication and verified TLS.

Other OAuth configurations

The default token_type = "EXT_JWT" uses an external provider’s JWT access token, as in the Entra example. To use an IAM Identity Center access token, set token_type = "ACCESS_TOKEN" and configure a shinyOAuth client that obtains it. Other identity providers can use their own shinyOAuth client with the same connection helper.

target = "redshift" selects the token target defined in the example client. Match that name to your client, or use target = NULL if your client has no named targets. Getting started explains these settings.
